audits.title: Improving Discharge Summary Follow-Up Documentation in a Major Trauma Center: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians Health Informatics Unit 2019 discharge summary content standards
audits.setting: Orthopaedic trauma ward, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust (major trauma centre)

cycle1.result: Follow-up plan fully detailed 15.6% (5/32); new medication indication documented 9.4% (3/32); patient advice fully detailed 21.2% (7/33); inpatient management fully detailed 30.3% (10/33).

audits.intervention: Educational poster with a checklist of RCP components, interactive teaching sessions, a discharge summary self-assessment checklist, reminders with one-to-one feedback for junior doctors and a team campaign (August to September 2025).

cycle2.result: Follow-up plan fully detailed 90.0% (18/20) (p < 0.0001); new medication indication 50.0% (9/18) (p = 0.004); patient advice fully detailed 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.0002); inpatient management fully detailed 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.001).

audits.other_findings: Any safety-net advice fell from 96.9% (32/33) to 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.02), though when present it was more often excellent. Seven-day readmission was 6.1% vs 4.8%, with no change.
audits.citation: Ahmed H, Mazhar F, Yousaf Z, Akram U, Mazhar S, Rizwan M. Improving Discharge Summary Follow-Up Documentation in a Major Trauma Center: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2025;17(12):e99842. doi:10.7759/cureus.99842. PMID: 41573452.

audits.standard: Local aim: increase discharge summary completion from 57.7% to 80% by June 2019
audits.setting: Gwent Specialist Substance Misuse Service, inpatient alcohol detoxes, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board

cycle1.result: Discharge summary completion rate 57.7%.

audits.intervention: PDSA cycle with process mapping, root cause analysis by brainstorming, education, communication and a checklist.

audits.setting: Functional old age psychiatry Wards 3 and 4, The Mount, Leeds

cycle1.result: Ward 3: 0 of 11 completed within 7 days; Ward 4: 23% of 13 met the target.

audits.intervention: Proposed dedicated 4-hour weekly slot for junior doctors, assigning a responsible doctor at discharge and a quiet onsite workspace.

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: Nine barriers were identified; lack of uninterrupted time and delayed doctor allocation were prioritised. The target was extended to 14 days.

audits.title: Improving Completion of Extended Discharge Documents (EDD) in a Forensic Psychiatry Service: A Baseline Audit and Reaudit Following System Change
audits.standard: National standards: Extended Discharge Document issued within 7-14 days of discharge
audits.setting: Forensic inpatient unit, Royal Cornhill Hospital, NHS Grampian

cycle1.result: 8/41 eligible discharges had a completed EDD (19.5%); 1 of these (12.5%) was delayed beyond 14 days.

audits.intervention: Each EDD assigned to a named doctor at discharge planning, standards reinforced at induction for rotating trainees, and a shared forensic handover template (digital and paper) to track outstanding EDDs.

cycle2.result: 22/27 completed (81.5%); completion above 75% every month and 100% in January. 16/22 (72.7%) issued more than 14 days after discharge.

audits.other_findings: Timeliness remained the key concern; early drafting, timeliness checkpoints and automated reminders proposed for the next cycle.

audits.title: An audit on sensitive documentation of suicide attempts and behaviour in Mount Carmel Hospital discharge summaries
audits.standard: International Association for Suicide Prevention (IASP) language guidelines
audits.setting: Mount Carmel Hospital (psychiatric hospital) discharge summaries

cycle1.result: 26% of included discharge letters did not use appropriate suicide-related terminology; commonest issues were excessive description of the attempt (53%) and 'commit suicide' (28%).

audits.intervention: Short presentation to foundation doctors on using sensitive language about suicide in discharge summaries.

cycle2.result: 20% of discharges did not use appropriate terminology (n = 34); use of 'commit suicide' fell significantly (OR 0.279; CI 0.0921 to 0.8452, p = 0.0240).

audits.other_findings: Sample sizes are total admissions screened; only discharges with suicidal behaviour were assessed.
audits.citation: Borg N, Gambin R, Gatt G, Cassar F. An audit on sensitive documentation of suicide attempts and behaviour in Mount Carmel Hospital discharge summaries. European Psychiatry. 2025;68(S1):S437-S438. doi:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2025.908.
